subject.size_in_frame: the bottle stands about 0.62 of frame height; the paper label round its neck is square-on and about 0.20 of frame height

headroom: about 0.16 of frame height between the bottle's stopper and the underside of the glass tabletop above — the tabletop is the lid of this frame, so the insert still knows which room it is in.
horizon_eyeline: Low from the floor at the curtain, lens 0.50 m: the tabletop plane runs across the top of frame at 0.14 of frame height and the flagstone line across the bottom at 0.92. The label plane is dead square-on to the lens and level.

layers.fg: her hands just entering frame from the right, fingertips only
layers.mg: the bottle and its label, sharp across the whole width of the lettering
layers.bg: the glass tabletop above and the dark hall beyond, falling away soft

gaze.note: no face in frame; the shot is an object and a hand.

balance: One vertical object on the exact centre line with symmetrical dark either side — the plainest possible framing, because the point is to read two words and nothing else.
leading_lines: The bottle's own shoulders and the two edges of the label form a tight horizontal band across the middle; the tabletop above is a long level line pressing down on it.
eye_first: The lettering, immediately — that is the whole function of the frame.
constraint_binding: DRINK ME gets exactly one clean legible read here: the label plane is square-on, unbroken by fingers, sharp across its whole width, and sits wholly inside title-safe (x 0.38-0.62, y 0.42-0.62) so no platform crop can clip the whitelisted lettering. Everywhere else in the episode the bottle is dressed, not hero-lit — so it takes the ordinary lamp key here, with no rim, no halo and no separate source.
